rounds.text: Krypton Industries exhibits a persistent inability to generate meaningful returns for shareholders, evidenced by a mediocre three-year median return on equity of just 4% [E25] and a five-year median of 5% [E24]. Despite recent profit volatility, the company’s long-term performance remains underwhelming, with compounded sales growth over five years stagnating at a mere 4% [E14]. Investors are currently paying a premium for these subpar returns, as the stock trades at a P/E of 17.7x and a P/B of 1.55x, both of which exceed their respective sector benchmarks [E6, E7]. Furthermore, the company’s share price has suffered a significant decline of 36% over the past year [E23], and it currently languishes at only 23% of its 52-week range [E5]. The low promoter holding of 26.3% [E49] and the fact that borrowings have increased to Rs 22.09 Cr [E37] add layers of risk to an already uninspiring capital efficiency profile. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong recent cash conversion [E31], significant short-term profit growth [E19], and expanding operating margins [E27].
